newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algerian court sentences 15 militants to death.
newsitem.headline: Algerian court sentences 15 militants to death.

text.p: An Algerian court sentenced 15 Moslem militants to death in absentia for their involvement in guerrilla activities, the official Algerian news agency APS said on Monday.

The criminal court in the northeastern town of Tizi-Ouzou, 90 km (60 miles) east of Algiers, on Sunday convicted the 15 militants of belonging to a "terrorist" group, on charges of manslaughter, carrying out ambushes, arson and holdups, said APS.
The court acquitted 15 other people tried on the same charges, APS added.
More than 1,000 Moslem militants have been sentenced to death, most of them in their absence, since 1993 when Algerian courts began trials of the activists.
About 60,000 people have been killed in violence in Algeria since the authorities in January 1992 cancelled a general election in which Moslem fundamentalists had taken a big lead.
Radical Islamists were barred from new elections held early this month but two Islamist-leaning parties were allowed to compete and won 103 seats in the 380-member National Assembly.
